claim: UPI moves about eighty crore payments a day (on-screen HUD: 80 CR / DAY [NPCI DATA | SEP 2026])
source_quote: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed 24.07 billion transactions worth Rs 29.37 lakh crore in September 2026, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
note: OUR CALCULATION: 24,068.38 million / 30 days = 802 million = about 80 crore a day. NPCI monthly table mirrored at https://dataful.in/datasets/431 (Sept 2026 total volume 24068.38 million). StartupTalky also reports average daily transactions crossing 800 million in Sept 2026. Re-check against npci.org.in statistics before render. VO v6 no longer says this number; it stays as the HUD UPI LOAD readout only.

claim: NPCI gives each bank fifteen seconds to reply a debit or credit request (on-screen: 15 S TIMEOUT [NPCI UPI CONSOLIDATED CIRCULAR | 2026])
source_quote: Request Pay, Response Pay (Debit and Credit) | Remitter Bank; Beneficiary Bank | 15 seconds
note: NPCI/UPI/CC/01 Version 1.0, section 12.1. Same 30 s to 15 s change reported by Mint (NPCI circular of 26 April 2025, effective 16 June 2025). Check Transaction Status and Reversal are 10 s; not in VO.

claim: The payment path: NPCI asks the payer's bank to debit; the bank debits and confirms; only then NPCI asks the payee's bank to credit; the payee's bank credits and confirms
source_quote: UPI sends the debit request to remitter bank 6. Remitter bank debits the remitter's account and sends confirmation to NPCI-UPI 7. NPCI-UPI sends credit request to beneficiary's bank 8. Beneficiary bank credits the customer's account and confirms the same to NPCI-UPI
note: World Bank Fast Payments Toolkit, source: NPCI and primary interviews. Same order in NPCI UPI Procedural Guidelines (2016): 'Remitter Bank debits the customer account ... UPI initiates credit request to the Beneficiary Bank'.

claim: When the shop's bank goes silent, NPCI stops waiting after the response time and marks the payment deemed (credit timeout), which the app shows as processing/pending
source_quote: UPI proactively triggers an API to the Remitter/Beneficiary Bank for checking and updating the status of pending transactions debit reversal timeout or deemed (credit timeout) transactions.
note: Section 32.3. 'Deemed' = credit timeout, which is the VO's wording.

claim: Answer two, RET (return): the shop never got it, the money goes back and your bank puts it in your account
source_quote: RET is where the Beneficiary Bank cannot process the credit to the User/customer account and returns the funds back to the Remitter

claim: Payment to a shop: money must come back within five days (on-screen: SHOP · T+5 DAYS [RBI CIRCULAR | 2019])
source_quote: Account debited but transaction confirmation not received at merchant location (payment to merchant). | Auto-reversal within T + 5 days. | ₹100/- per day if delay is beyond T + 5 days.
note: RBI/2019-20/67, Harmonisation of TAT, 20 Sept 2019, in force 15 Oct 2019; NPCI consolidated circular 2026 section 31 still binds members to it.

claim: Sent to a person: back by the next day (on-screen: PERSON · T+1 DAY [RBI CIRCULAR | 2019])
source_quote: Account debited but the beneficiary account is not credited (transfer of funds). | If unable to credit the beneficiary account, auto reversal (R) by the Beneficiary bank latest on T + 1 day.
note: Note 4 of the circular: 'T is the day of transaction and refers to the calendar date', so 'the next day' is a calendar day.

claim: Miss the deadline and the bank pays you one hundred rupees for every extra day (on-screen: ₹100 / DAY)
source_quote: ₹100/- per day if delay is beyond T + 1 day.
Wherever financial compensation is involved, the same shall be effected to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim from the customer.
note: If it is not paid, the customer can complain to the RB-IOS 2021 (same circular, para 6); not in VO, can go in the pinned comment.

claim: Never pay again while it says processing: if the answer is T.C.C. (the shop was credited), you have paid twice
note: Advice, not law. A pending payment can still end as success, so paying again risks paying twice. NPCI requires apps to show transaction status and let users raise a complaint (UDIR, consolidated circular 32.5).

claim: A UPI app shows one of three statuses: success, failed, or processing (some apps say pending) (on-screen: SUCCESS · FAILED · PROCESSING)
source_quote: Pending Payment Initiated Confirmation Awaited Payment Processing … Failed Payment Initiated Kindly Try Again Payment Failed … Approved or Pending Failed
note: NPCI UPI Help brand guidelines (July 2023): transaction history screens show Approved / Pending / Failed; the pending screen reads Payment Processing, Confirmation Awaited. App wording varies (Successful, Pending, Processing), which the VO says.

claim: Failed: the shop's bank picks up and says no (for example a problem with the shop's account); your money already left, so NPCI tells your bank to give it back
source_quote: P2P Failed U005 Customer account not credited back for failed P2P transaction … P2M Failed U009 Customer account not credited back for failed merchant transaction
note: NPCI complaint codes exist for failed payments where the debit was not reversed, so a failed payment can carry a debit that must come back; RBI TAT circular (U08-U10) sets the deadline. Declines such as a wrong PIN are rejected before any debit (Axis Bank UPI response codes: RM Invalid Mpin, REJECTED).

claim: Failed is the safe one: just pay again; processing means wait, never pay again
source_quote: 04 Technical Decline REJECTED Reinitiate with same CRN … 091 Timeout PENDING Do not re-initiate
note: Axis Bank's UPI response-code table marks declined (failed) payments 'Reinitiate' and timeouts 'PENDING, Do not re-initiate'. NPCI's failed screen also reads 'Kindly Try Again' (U13).

claim: UPI runs on two layers: messages in real time; the money between banks settles later in batches, ten cycles a day, through the banks' settlement accounts at the RBI (on-screen: 10 BATCHES / DAY [NPCI UPI CIRCULAR | 2026])
source_quote: The payment obligations and settlement instructions among the Members shall be determined through netting … the settlement account of all the Members that are in net debit position is debited and settlement account of all the Members in net credit position is credited, through Multilateral Net Settlement Batch (MNSB) in the Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system … Annexure E – UPI Settlement Cycles: cycles 1 to 10
note: NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 (18 Sep 2026), section 29 and Annexure E: 10 settlement cycles (21:00-00:00, 00:00-05:00, then every 2 hours 05:00-21:00) plus dispute cycles DC1/DC2. NPCI OC 222 (2025-26): cycles 1 to 10 carry authorised transactions only. Settlement accounts are held with the RBI (World Bank case study: "net settlement position is passed to RBI's RTGS for settlement through accounts maintained by members with RBI").

claim: On a credit timeout NPCI marks the payment deemed approved and settles it the same as approved, so in the next batch the money moves from your bank to the shop's bank
source_quote: Deemed Approved: In case of time out from the RMA/beneficiary bank then NPCI shall treat such transactions as deemed approved and process the settlement same as approved. The participants are expected to complete the reconciliation in offline mode on T+1 day
note: NPCI UPI Global QR rules as issued by the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan (2024); the Indian side is the same UPI scheme: NPCI OC 213 (10 Feb 2025) refers to "UPI deemed approved transactions" on which beneficiary banks must "reconcile and process returns (RET)/TCC", and the RBI TAT table puts the reversal on the Beneficiary bank (U09), which is consistent with the money sitting there.

claim: The next day the shop's bank checks its books and must file one of two answers: TCC (credited) or RET (return)
source_quote: beneficiary banks are not getting sufficient time to reconcile and process returns (RET)/TCC proactively … the chargeback has been closed on deemed acceptance basis along with RBI penalty
note: NPCI OC 213/2024-25. Timing: NPCI consolidated circular list item OC 42 "Enhanced penalty for not updating TCC, RET, DRC & RRC after T+1 working days"; section 32.9: manual entries for pending transactions on T+1, not T+0. RMA rules: "reconciliation in offline mode on T+1 day". TCC = transaction credit confirmation.

claim: Answer one (TCC) can mean the shop has the money even though its speaker stayed silent
source_quote: Deemed (TCC-102): Merchant account credited online but failed to respond online to RMA and NPCI.
note: Basis for the tip to check the bank statement, not the speaker. The soundbox announcement depends on the confirmation that never arrived (film 03 covers how the speaker works).

claim: Stuck after the deadline? Complain in your app's UPI Help
source_quote: Beneficiary account is not credited for a pending / timeout transaction … Complaint Raised Successfully Complaint Reference number
note: NPCI UPI Help (UDIR) complaint flow in the app; consolidated circular 31-32 requires members to run grievance redressal and UDIR. Beyond the bank: RBI TAT circular para 6, complain to the RBI Integrated Ombudsman (on screen in the description or pinned comment).

claim: When the shop's bank explicitly declines, NPCI sends your bank a reversal (the "give it back" call)
source_quote: Transaction Reversal (Debit and Credit) | Remitter Bank; Beneficiary Bank | 10 seconds
note: NPCI consolidated circular 12.1: reversal is its own API with a 10-second response time. Beneficiary-side decline reasons include closed or frozen accounts (NPCI UPI Procedural Guidelines 2016: "Wrong Credits / Closed / Frozen Accounts"). The RBI TAT rule (U08-U10) covers any debit that does not come back.
